claim: November5 closeout: long CAD/NOK remains a conditional research candidate and is deprioritized, not entered. The five-observation oil decline produced only about0.08% cross appreciation, while the election-day cross rose0.26%. That weakens a prompt relative-energy-premium unwind thesis; calling the positive day itself a failure overstates the evidence. Norges' retained hike option is contrary context and a slower adjustment remains possible. No stable relative oil sensitivity, NOK policy comparison or independently justified target has been established. This is not a blanket no-forward-points ban; missing costs should be handled with labeled sensitivities when defensible. Retain the previously conditional prospective forecast and its actual stated_at unchanged; the November4 closes predate it and are not forecast performance. The prior percentile correction remains:0.03968 on a0–100 scale was about the0.04th percentile.

competing_explanations.statement: The five-year extreme may reflect a structural relative-rate, fiscal or external-balance change rather than a temporary energy premium.
CAD may weaken more than NOK when oil falls; a shared producer label does not establish relative beta.
Broad risk-on can support both currencies with changing relative effects. A stable historical correlation is not assumed.
The observed rise may be broad risk/USD repricing or the entire tactical reversal already realized; one daily cross return does not identify oil causality.
Norges' retained hike option could sustain NOK policy support despite cheaper oil. A complete relative policy comparison remains necessary.
NOK strength may reflect structural or policy support rather than a temporary energy premium; the oil-down week did not identify a reliable relative-beta reversal.

falsifiers.statement: NOK outperformance persists during sustained oil declines, contradicting the assumed relative energy transmission.
Relative policy or growth repricing favors NOK enough to offset any energy-premium reversal.
The next common packet shows the cross already repriced sufficiently that the residual expected reward no longer compensates the downside and financing.
